newsitem.title: USA: Charleston, W.Va., mayor seeks $12.5 mln in bonds.
newsitem.headline: Charleston, W.Va., mayor seeks $12.5 mln in bonds.

text.p: Charleston, W.Va., Mayor Kemp Melton has proposed bond financing for all or part of four projects totalling $12.5 million,, the Daily Mail said Thursday.
The mayor is seeking $6.5 million for civic center renovations. The rest of the money would be used to build a new police headquarters, a public service precinct office and a recreation complex.

City officials have identified $650,000 in motel tax, coal severance payments and amusement tax revenues that could be used to pay debt service on about $8.5 million worth of revenue bonds issued for the projects, the newspaper said.
The city is reviewing whether to use certificates of participation or pay-as-you-go funding for the rest.
The newspaper said Melton and City Manager Bill Kenny would meet with city council members later in the week to discuss the projects.
